security.title: Security Setup
security.description: Quickly configure your server to use the bot's advanced moderation system.

sections.title: Antinuke
sections.subtitle: Impose restrictions on moderators to prevent destructive behavior.

overview.why: It's important to have an antinuke system in place to prevent moderators from abusing their permissions. This is a security measure which lets your server stay safe from any harmful actions.
overview.how: The antinuke will set a limit on the number of actions a moderator can perform in a certain time frame. If the limit is exceeded, the moderator will be punished and a message will be sent to the owner.

configuration.note: Discord recently implemented a new mass ban feature which can quickly ban 100+ members. It's HIGHLY recommended to utilize fake permissions to prevent moderators from using this feature.

access.initial: Only the server owner can configure the antinuke
access.admins: Use ,antinuke admin @user to allow others to configure

commands.name: antinuke admin
commands.description: Allow users to configure the antinuke
commands.warning: This is a dangerous command and will allow the user to entirely alter the antinuke configuration.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User to grant antinuke admin permissions

commands.name: antinuke whitelist
commands.warning: This is a dangerous command and will allow the user to bypass the antinuke entirely.

flags.threshold: Number of bans allowed before punishment (1-10)
flags.punishment: Action to take: strip (remove roles), kick, or ban

commands.name: antinuke botadd
notes: No threshold needed for botadd module

commands.name: antinuke permissions
notes: Automatically watches 9 dangerous permissions when enabled

commands.name: antinuke list
commands.description: View enabled modules and whitelisted users

commands.name: antinuke admins
commands.description: View users with antinuke admin permissions

moderation.title: Moderation
moderation.description: Guide to setting up moderation commands in your server.

sections.title: Moderation Setup
sections.overview: Moderation commands require some basic setup before they can be used. This includes moderation logs, mute roles, and the jailed role & channel.

steps.title: Creating the case logs & jail role
steps.description: Jail is a feature similar to mute, but it restricts users from all channels except #jail.
creates: Case logs channel - Logs all moderation actions
#jail channel - Where jailed members can talk

steps.title: Creating the necessary mute roles
steps.description: This will create a text mute, image mute, and reaction mute role.
creates: Muted - Used to restrict users from sending messages
Image Muted - Used to restrict users from uploading attachments
Reaction Muted - Used to restrict users from reacting to messages
Jailed - Used to restrict users from all channels except the #jail channel

notes: The jailed role cannot be renamed since it's found by its name
The #jail-log channel logs all moderation actions done through the bot
The #jail channel is where users jailed by the jail command are restricted to

commands.name: setup
commands.description: Create case logs channel and jail role

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: Manage various role systems in your server.

sections.title: Booster Roles
sections.subtitle: Reward your boosters with unique roles for themselves.
sections.overview: Booster roles are unique roles that are given to members which have boosted your server. These roles can be fully customized by the members themselves.

setup.title: Setting the base role
setup.description: In order for the booster roles to work, you must set a base role. All booster roles will be placed under this role.
setup.note: The base role should be a role which is above any roles with a color, otherwise the color won't be visible due to Discord's role hierarchy.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Hex color code or color name

sections.title: Reaction Roles
sections.subtitle: Allow your members to assign themselves roles by reacting to a message.
sections.overview: Reaction roles are roles that are assigned to members when they react to a message. This can be useful for letting members choose unique roles or as a way to verify themselves.

commands.name: reactionrole add

parameters.name: message link
parameters.description: Link to the message (right-click > Copy Message Link)

notes: You can create multiple reaction roles for a single message
Use different emojis for each role

commands.name: reactionrole removeall
commands.description: Remove all reaction roles for a message
notes: This is different from reactionrole reset which removes all reaction roles from the server

commands.name: reactionrole reset
commands.description: Remove all reaction roles from the server
commands.warning: This CAN NOT be undone and will remove ALL reaction roles from the server.

useCases.title: Verification System
useCases.description: Reaction roles can be used to create a verification system where members must react to a message to gain access to the server.
useCases.note: In order for this to work, you'll need to create a role that will be assigned to members when they react to the message, such as a Member role.

sections.title: Auto Roles
sections.description: Automatically assign roles when members join.

embedScripting.title: Embed Scripting
embedScripting.description: Learn how to build embeds and use variables for your server's configurations.

overview.what: Embeds are rich message formats that allow you to display information in a structured, visually appealing way with colors, images, fields, and more.
overview.structure: Embeds use a key-value pair structure where each parameter is separated by a colon and parameters are separated by $v.

syntax.usage: Some commands accept both raw text and embed code. When using embeds, prefix your code with {embed}$v

basic.name: description
basic.description: Sets the main content/body of the embed
notes: Press SHIFT + ENTER to add new lines

basic.name: color
basic.description: Sets the embed's side color bar (use hex color codes)

basic.name: url
basic.description: Makes the title clickable with a link

basic.name: image
basic.description: Adds a large image at the bottom of the embed

basic.name: thumbnail
basic.description: Adds a small image in the top-right corner

basic.name: timestamp
basic.description: Adds a timestamp at the bottom (uses current time, no arguments needed)

author.description: Displays information at the top of the embed with optional icon and link

footer.description: Displays text and optional icon at the bottom of the embed

field.description: Fields allow you to display information in organized columns

parameters.name: inline
parameters.description: Add this to make field display side-by-side with others

button.description: Add interactive buttons to your embeds

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Button URL (for Link type) or emoji

buttonTypes.name: Link
buttonTypes.description: Opens a URL (requires valid https:// URL)

examples.code: {button: Link && Website && https://example.com && enabled}$v{button: Link && Support && https://discord.gg/support && enabled}$v{button: Green && Join && 🎉 && enabled}

overview.description: Variables are dynamic placeholders that get replaced with actual data when messages are sent. They use the format {category.property}.
overview.usage: Simply include variables in your text or embed code
